HYPOTHESIS (final, data-grounded)

In ML-enabled system projects, the two roles most strongly associated with requirements are the Project Lead / Project Manager and the Data Scientist: they are by far the most frequently cited roles as the ones who address requirements/ML aspects in practitioners' organizations (Q8 multi-select). In our canonical analysis over the 194 respondents who answered the Q8 block, Project Lead/Project Manager is cited by 51.03% of respondents (99/194; bootstrap 95% CI [43.81, 58.25]) and Data Scientist by 48.97% (95/194; 95% CI [41.75, 56.19]), while the third-ranked Business Analyst trails at 25.77% (95% CI [19.59, 31.96]) — a clearly separated top-2 that is invariant across all 20+ subset/denominator variants tested (e.g., Completed-only 49.39%/49.39%; Completed+after-break 51.06%/49.47%; share-of-citations 30.3%/29.1%). The finding supports the hypothesis that requirements for ML-enabled systems are handled predominantly by project leadership and data scientists rather than by dedicated requirements engineers (cited by only 10.31% of respondents), i.e., requirements engineering for ML is largely absorbed into existing, non-RE-specific roles.

WORKFLOW EXECUTED (summary)
1. Load CSV (276×202, unique IDs); per-cell validity mask: -77/-99/-66/'0' treated as non-response, excluded from numerator and denominator; 194 respondents answered Q8 (82/88 Suspended rows have the whole Q8 block = -77).
2. Verified Q8_ML_Addressing_* is binary multi-select ("quoted"/"not quoted"), not Likert; association proportion = quoted/(quoted+not quoted).
3. Bootstrap: resample respondents with replacement, 10,000 replicates, 95% percentile CI per role; Wilson score interval as sanity check (agrees).
4. Broad scan: 12 subset/denominator variants × 8 roles (96 estimates) + the additional bounded deterministic scan commissioned now (see RECONCILIATION below).
5. Final top-2 table with bootstrap CIs under canonical and Completed-only variants.

RECONCILIATION SCAN (the commissioned bounded, deterministic check)
(a) Denominator 276 treating -77 as 'not quoted' (and all negative codes as 'not quoted'): Project Lead 35.87%, Data Scientist 34.42% — no hit.
(b) Conditional on citers of ≥1 named role (Others excluded): n=164 (all rows: PL 60.37%, DS 57.93%); Completed-only × ge1-named: n=139 (PL=DS 58.27%); Completed+after-break × ge1-named: n=161 (PL 61.49%, DS 58.39%) — closest approach to 61.389% yet (distance 0.10 pt) but not within ±0.05 pt, and it is a conditional denominator that also leaves Data Scientist at 58.4%, inconsistent with the reference pair.
(c) Conditional on valid D4_Role (excluding '0' and 'Other'): PL 56.12%, DS 53.96% — no hit.
(d) Full grid condition × status × -77 treatment (7 base masks × 2 treatments, each also crossed with the ge1-named condition, with both -77 treatments): no estimate within ±0.05 pt of either reference value.
(e) Share-of-citations (role citations / total citations): PL 28.61% of 346 total citations (30.28% of the 327 named-role citations), DS 27.46%/29.05%; share-of-valid-cells (k/1552): ~6.4%/6.1% — no hit.
(f) Integer-fraction search (k/N, N∈[100,400]): no (k, N) with N∈{164,188,194,276} reproduces 61.389% (closest achievable at our real denominators: 119/194 = 61.340%, 0.049 pt off, but no role has 119 citations; at N=164: 101/164 = 61.585%, no role matches); 49.6% is exactly 62/125 (=124/250, 186/375) — denominators that do not correspond to any respondent/citation count in this dataset; the closest real counts are 93/188 = 49.468% and 81/164 = 81/164 = 49.390%.
CONCLUSION OF SCAN: no variant reproduces 49.6% or 61.389% (±0.05 pt) for any role. Per the agreed closure rule, the final hypothesis stands with the n=194 canonical figures, and the 61.389% (and its ~±0.4-pt CI) is documented as non-reproducible from the supplied data — the reference values and their implausibly tight CIs (incompatible with a respondent-level bootstrap at n≈194, which yields ~±7-pt CIs) most plausibly originate from the source publication's own sample and processing rather than from this CSV.

LIMITATIONS
- 61.389% reference value not reproducible under any tested aggregation; documented above with the closest candidates.
- Q8 is multi-select, so proportions do not sum to 100% and answers within a respondent are correlated (handled by respondent-level resampling).
- Q8_Others free text kept as a separate category in the canonical pipeline; redistributing clearly-named mentions moves Project Lead to 55.67% without changing the ranking.
- The tight reference CIs cannot arise from respondent-level bootstrapping of a proportion at n≈194; they likely come from the publication's own analysis, limiting exact numeric reconciliation.

payload.hypothesis: The two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems are Project Lead/Project Manager (51.03% of the 194 valid respondents, bootstrap 95% CI [43.81, 58.25]) and Data Scientist (48.97%, 95% CI [41.75, 56.19]); both clearly exceed the third-ranked Business Analyst (25.77%), supporting the hypothesis that requirements for ML-enabled systems are predominantly handled by project leadership and data scientists rather than dedicated requirements engineers (cited by only 10.31%). The reference value 61.389% (95% CI [60.955, 61.822]) could not be reproduced from the supplied CSV under any of ~20 tested aggregations and is documented as a limitation; the qualitative top-2 conclusion is invariant.
payload.workflow: 1) Load CSV (276x202, unique IDs); per-cell validity mask excluding -77/-99/-66/'0' as non-response; 194 respondents answered Q8. 2) Verified Q8 is binary multi-select ('quoted'/'not quoted'); proportion = quoted/(quoted+not quoted). 3) Bootstrap: respondent-level resampling, 10,000 replicates, 95% percentile CI per role; Wilson interval sanity check. 4) Broad scan of 12 subset/denominator variants (96 estimates) plus the commissioned bounded deterministic scan: denominator-276 with negatives-as-not-quoted; ge1-named-role conditioning (all/completed/completed+break; both -77 treatments); D4-valid conditioning; full condition x status x treatment grid; share-of-citations and share-of-valid-cells; integer-fraction search k/N (N in 100..400). Result: NO variant reproduces 49.6% or 61.389% within ±0.05 pt (closest: PL 61.49% at n=161 conditional; DS 49.47% at n=188). Top-2 (Project Lead/PM, Data Scientist) invariant across all variants; final hypothesis uses canonical n=194 figures with non-reproducibility of 61.389% documented as limitation.
